title: WCode materializes application resources declared in canonical Pkl
persona: assistant building and running a Windows Swift application through Vaporize WCode
steps: The assistant explicitly selects WCode with a package path, safe single-component product, target, platform, and configuration.
WCode resolves project.pkl and evaluates it through PklSwift against the canonical project-definition contract.
WCode selects exactly one target and plans its first-class resources independently from Xcode/PBX source build phases.
The resource service validates every package-relative source and resource-root-relative destination before writing.
The service stages copy resources in a temporary sibling, refuses collisions and unsupported processing, then publishes the complete resource root.
WCode exposes the resource root to the built application and records per-resource outcomes in the lifecycle receipt.

Installation remains inside the admitted per-user Programs root and copies only the selected executable, canonical resource root, and exact runtime artifact names explicitly admitted with repeated --wcode-runtime-artifact options.
No PowerShell process or lifecycle script participates in build, staging, installation, or launch.
failureJourneys: A source or destination attempts to escape its allowed root.
Two declarations resolve to the same destination.
A process mode or filter contract is not implemented.
The selected target or platform is absent or ambiguous.
The product or runtime artifact is not one safe Windows filename component.
The install destination is not a strict descendant of the admitted per-user Programs root.
A caller attempts to overwrite a reserved WCODE_ environment value.
